 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR PANDEY
ORAL ORDER 9 13-09-2024
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State on I.A. No.02/2023 which has been filed for grant of bail and suspension of sentence.

2. The present appeal has been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 24.01.2020 and order of sentence dated 31.01.2020 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-1st, Supaul passed in connection with Sessions Case No. 363/2018 arising out of Bhimpur P.S. Case No. 59/2018,
whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years and a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- (one lac) which will be paid to the victim.
3. As per prosecution case, the appellant is said to have committed rape upon the informant/victim.
Patna High Court CR.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits the earlier bail prayer of the present appellant has already been rejected on merit by this Court on 27.03.2023 with an observation that the appellant may renew his prayer for bail after nine months, if the appeal is not taken up for hearing.

He further Makhan Safi @ Mohammad Safi vs The State Of Bihar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176877326/
1 submits that the appellant is in custody since 10.09.2018.

sentences.text: The medical evidence does not corroborate the story of prosecution and P.W.-4 has stated that the said case has been registered on account of pressure tactics by the people in the light of fact that they surrounded the police station.

He further submits that there is no eye witness to the alleged occurrence except the informant/victim.
5.

Learned A.P.P. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer of bail of the appellant and submits that earlier bail prayer of the present appellant has already been rejected on merit by this Court on 27.03.2023.

He further submits that the victim/informant herself has supported the case of prosecution and judgment of conviction and order of sentence has been passed by the concerned court is on the due appreciation of evidences.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, particularly keeping in view that earlier bail prayer of the appellant has been rejected on merit as well as coupled with the material available on record, I am not inclined to grant bail to the appellant.
Hence, I.A. No. 02/2023 stands rejected.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1262 of 2020(9) dt.13-09-2024 7.
However, the appellant may renew his prayer for bail after six months, if the appeal is not taken up for hearing.

(Alok Kumar Pandey, J) amitkumar/-
